chunks: From him, from Abū ʿAbdillāh al-Rāzī, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Sayf ibn ʿUmayrah, from ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar, the client of the Anṣār: that he asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man—whether it is permissible for him to shake hands with a Magian. So he said:
"No." Then he asked him, "Should he perform wudu (ablution) if he shakes hands with them?" He said, "Yes. Indeed, shaking hands with them invalidates the wudu (ablution)."

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: This report is to be understood as referring to the washing of the hand, and that may be called wudu, as we have explained, because when a Muslim shakes hands with a kāfir, washing his hand becomes obligatory upon him, as we have explained.

key_terms.ٱلْمَجُوسِيَّ: the Magian; a Zoroastrian referred to in the legal question
key_terms.ٱلْوُضُوءَ: wudu (ablution), here explained contextually as hand-washing

ai.seo_question: Does shaking hands with a non-Muslim invalidate wudu (ablution) in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling on shaking hands with a Magian and mentions wudu (ablution) afterward. Shaykh al-Ṭūsī explains that the report should be understood as referring to washing the hand rather than the nullification of ritual wudu (ablution), clarifying the legal implication in matters of taharah (ritual purity).
